title: Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers — What Science Actually Says #Shorts
description:
Meaning is not found in Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers — it is manufactured for it. Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers is a 1995 American slasher film directed by Joe Chappelle, written by Daniel Farrands, and starring Donald Pleasence, Paul Rudd, Marianne Hagan, and Mitch Ryan. The sequel to Halloween 5: The Revenge of Michael Myers and the sixth installment in the Halloween film series, the plot depicts Michael Myers hunting down the infant son of his niece, Jamie Lloyd.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers shows exactly where that breaks. Farrands expanded on the presence of the "Man in Black" in Halloween 5 as well as the appearance of the Thorn symbol, both of which appear without explanation at the end of Halloween 5. When beginning the script, Farrands contacted the writers of Halloween 4 and 5 for additional information, but they were unable to provide clear answers, leaving him to "pick up the pieces".
